name: Sonnet global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
strategy: Rotate the core toward international/EM ETFs and quality non-US ADRs that lagged the US AI-infra rally, keep crypto exposure at zero given the deep bear trend, and hold a modest inverse-ETF hedge plus elevated cash against US mega-cap AI-valuation risk.

positions.thesis: Broad EM ETF core exposure; trimmed slightly since the fund is ~46% tech-weighted (TSM 15%, Samsung 8% of NAV) and thus more AI-capex-correlated than a clean EM diversifier.
Best-in-class semis ADR, trimmed after -13.34%/mo AI-selloff; still a core long-term holding but sized down given confirmed near-term AI-capex de-rating risk.
Monopoly lithography maker, trimmed after -13.59%/mo drop on China-competition fears; BofA calls the reaction overdone and it's still +44.6% YTD, so kept as a smaller position rather than exited.
Brazil ETF, low correlation to the US AI-valuation trade; unchanged conviction.
Japan ETF, governance-reform tailwind independent of US tech drawdown; unchanged.
China ADR, added to on continued resilience (+21.33%/mo) despite weak cash-flow headlines -- stimulus/e-commerce recovery optionality thesis playing out.
India ETF, structural EM growth diversification, low correlation to the current US AI-capex selloff; modestly increased.

Tactical hedge against US AI-infra valuation correction, upsized meaningfully because the correction is now visibly underway (SQQQ +29.56%/mo, S&P -2.44%/wk on hawkish Fed shock) -- this is the mandate's core hedge doing its job.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The book's own thesis -- an AI-infra valuation correction -- is confirming live: Fed-hawkish-driven risk-off (S&P -1.52% on the day, VIX +13.45%) is hitting AI-capex names hardest (TSM -13.34%/mo, ASML -13.59%/mo) while the SQQQ hedge has surged +29.56%/mo. Rather than rebuild the book, I'm resizing: trimming the two most AI-capex-correlated longs (TSM, ASML) that are driving the drawdown, trimming EEM slightly since it is itself ~46% tech-weighted with TSM/Samsung as top holdings (a weaker diversifier than its label suggests), adding to BABA which has held up well (+21.33%/mo, stimulus/recovery thesis intact) and to EWZ/INDA which remain low-correlation to the US AI trade, and roughly tripling the SQQQ hedge since it is doing exactly what the mandate designed it to do in exactly this kind of tape. Gross exposure and cash held flat at 80/20 given still-elevated volatility -- this is a rotation within the existing risk budget, not a leverage-up.
research_notes: WebSearch budget was exhausted session-wide, so research was done via WebFetch on Yahoo Finance quote pages (data as of close 7/27-7/28/2026, the most recent available). Key findings: (1) Broad market risk-off in progress -- S&P500 -1.52% on the day, -2.44%/wk, VIX +13.45%, triggered by hawkish Fed comments from Chair Kevin Warsh ('Wall Street's worst day since April 2025'). (2) AI/semis-capex names getting hit hardest: TSM -11.05%/wk, -13.34%/mo; ASML -13.94%/wk, -13.59%/mo (China lithography-competition fears, though BofA calls it an overreaction and ASML is still +44.64% YTD); leveraged semis SOXL -42.86%/wk, -61.11%/mo (extreme, largely already played out). (3) SQQQ (my Round-2 inverse-Nasdaq hedge) is up +20.76%/wk, +29.56%/mo -- the book's own 'AI-valuation-correction' hedge thesis is confirmed live. (4) EEM is heavily AI/semis-correlated itself (tech 45.88% of fund, TSM 15.05%, Samsung 8.14%), down -7.19%/mo -- less of a clean diversifier than intended. (5) BABA is resilient, +21.33%/mo despite weak op-cash-flow headlines -- stimulus/e-commerce-recovery thesis holding up. (6) For Round 3: financials (XLF) show confirmed momentum, +7.52%/mo, +2.66%/wk, at 52-week highs; biotech (XBI) is still +23.62% YTD ('biotech is booming' per multiple outlets, Alzheimer's/weight-loss catalysts active) despite a recent -6.56%/mo pullback; gold miners (GDX) are underperforming gold itself (GDX -15.28% YTD vs GLD -6.37% YTD, gold spot near $4,126/oz) and still sliding (-4.06%/wk) -- a live mean-reversion short; SOXL has already crashed -61%/mo so a fresh short there is late and carries real squeeze risk, sized small with a hard stop accordingly. Also noted: the current Round-3 book (EFA/NVS/RIO/UL/EWU/EWW/EMB) does not resemble the stated Round-3 mandate (domestic biotech/financials long vs gold-miner/leveraged-semis short) at all -- it reads like a duplicate of the Round-2 international-diversification book. Realigned Round 3 to its actual mandate this round.
